topic.title: Elite C++ Mechanics
topic.description: SFINAE, Template Metaprogramming, Memory Models, Strict Aliasing, and Deep Language Quirks.

questions.title: SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error)
questions.explanation: test<HasFoo>(0) successfully substitutes T and finds void foo(), returning the int 1. test<NoFoo>(0) fails to substitute (no foo() found), so SFINAE discards the first template and falls back to the catch-all test(...) which returns the char '0'.

questions.title: Placement New
questions.explanation: Placement new constructs an object at a pre-allocated memory address (buffer). It calls the constructor (C). We then print 42. Since it wasn't allocated with standard 'new', we must explicitly call the destructor (D).

questions.title: Strict Aliasing Rule Violation
questions.explanation: While this is technically undefined behavior due to breaking strict aliasing (accessing an object through a pointer to a different type), in practice on a little-endian machine, it reads the least significant 2 bytes (0x5678).

questions.title: Vector Reallocation Invalidating Iterators
questions.explanation: When a vector exceeds its capacity, it allocates a new memory block and moves the elements. Any pointers, references, or iterators to the old elements (like p) are invalidated. Thus the new address is different.

questions.title: Constexpr if (C++17)
questions.explanation: constexpr if evaluates the condition at compile time. check(a) evaluates the else branch (V) and discards the if branch. check(&a) evaluates the if branch (P) and discards the else branch.

questions.title: Reference Collapsing Rules
questions.explanation: When an lvalue (a) is passed to a forwarding reference (T&&), T deduces as int&. int& && collapses to int& (L). When an rvalue (5) is passed, T deduces as int. int && remains int&& (R).

questions.title: Virtual Table Pointer Size
questions.explanation: An empty class typically has size 1 byte. A class with a virtual function must store a hidden vptr (virtual table pointer), meaning its size is usually 8 bytes (on 64-bit systems). Thus, it's larger.

questions.title: Exception Specifications (noexcept)
questions.explanation: The noexcept operator checks at compile time whether an expression is declared to not throw any exceptions. safe() is 1 (true), unsafe() is 0 (false).

questions.title: Template Metaprogramming (Factorial)
questions.explanation: This recursively evaluates 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 * 1 entirely at compile time using template specialization.

questions.title: Pointers to Members
questions.explanation: ptr is a pointer-to-member of class C. It stores the offset of member 'y'. When dereferenced on instance 'obj' using the .* operator, it retrieves obj.y (20).

questions.title: Sequence Points and Undefined Behavior
questions.explanation: Modifying a variable multiple times without an intervening sequence point invokes undefined behavior. It could output anything or crash, but we print 'UB' conceptually.

questions.title: Currying with std::bind
questions.explanation: std::bind maps the first argument (1) to 'a', hardcodes 2 for 'b', and maps the second argument (3) to 'c'.

questions.title: Data Padding and Alignment
questions.explanation: Both structs typically require 8 bytes. A: 1 byte char + 3 bytes padding + 4 bytes int. B: 4 bytes int + 1 byte char + 3 bytes padding at the end to align the struct array. So they are equal (1).

questions.title: Bit Fields
questions.explanation: b is a 2-bit unsigned field (max value 3). When it is 3 and 1 is added, it overflows to 0. a remains 1.

questions.title: Covariant Return Types
questions.explanation: A derived class overriding a virtual function can return a pointer/reference to a derived type instead of the base type. Dynamic dispatch ensures the Derived clone is called.

questions.title: Move semantics on returning local objects
questions.explanation: By explicitly calling std::move(o), you PREVENT the compiler from performing NRVO (Named Return Value Optimization). Instead, it forces a move construction (M) into the return value.

questions.title: Multiple Inheritance Ambiguity
questions.explanation: d.f() would be ambiguous because both L and R have f(). However, using the scope resolution operator explicitly calls L's version.

questions.title: std::launder
questions.explanation: Because 'n' is const, reusing its memory with placement new without std::launder leads to UB when reading. std::launder provides a pointer to the newly created object, returning 2.

questions.title: Default Member Initializers vs Member Initializer List
questions.explanation: If a member is initialized both in the default member initializer (1) and in the constructor's member initializer list (2), the constructor's list takes precedence.

questions.title: Destructor of Temporary Objects
questions.explanation: The temporary object T() is created, p() is called printing 'P'. The temporary is destroyed at the end of the full expression (the semicolon), printing 'D'. Then 'E' is printed.

questions.title: Template Template Parameters
questions.explanation: The function takes a container that itself takes a type and an allocator. std::vector matches this signature. It correctly prints the size 3.

questions.title: Exception catching order
questions.explanation: Catch blocks are evaluated in order. Since MyExc inherits from std::exception, the first block (std::exception&) catches it, printing S. The second block is never reached.

questions.title: sizeof with side effects
questions.explanation: The operand of sizeof is not evaluated at runtime (except for VLAs in C). Therefore, a++ is never executed, and 'a' remains 1.

questions.title: Volatile keyword
questions.explanation: Volatile tells the compiler not to optimize away reads. It reads 5 into a, then reads 5 into b. They are equal. Output is 1.

questions.title: Trailing Return Types
questions.explanation: The trailing return type uses decltype(a + b). int + double results in double. sizeof(double) is typically 8 bytes.
